effect: Anger over a sovereign default now fades. While a country stayed in default it paid a flat 12 points of approval and 10 of stability, on top of the one-off hit, for as long as the default lasted. Public anger peaks and then fades. The penalty now halves each year down to a quarter of its size, which remains until the default ends: at the moment of default it is the same as before, after a year 62.5%, after two 44%. A country that starts the game in default has no default day and counts from day 0. The half-life and the residue are a tuning choice from the direction of the evidence, not a measured rate. Expected effect: long-defaulted countries recover some approval and stability, and start fewer crises from that term alone. Day 0 unchanged. No new state. (Minified names in this text are those of build 26403824; the patch's find text has the current ones.)
